title: Departure Signal Triage & Counterfactuals Workbook
body:
Purpose:
Provide a lightweight, execution-ready workbook for triaging customer departure signals, constructing timelines for QBRs, and designing counterfactual experiments to reduce future churn. This is intentionally operational and short-form — use in weekly CS ops, QBR prep, and post-mortem writeups.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise and mid-market renewal risks (>$10k ARR).
- Signals covered: renewal decline, sudden drop in usage, repeated support escalations, product misalignment, security/regulatory blockers, and competitive displacement.
- Not a sales playbook — focused on root cause capture, testable counterfactuals, and an ownerable action backlog.

Quick triage checklist (first 48h):
1) Validate signal provenance: renewal notice, monitoring alert, CSM flag, AE email, or executive slack. Note timestamp and source.
2) Gather owner roster: CSM, AE, Solutions Eng, TAM, Product PM. Assign single primary owner.
3) Pull key artifacts: last 12 months of usage metrics, support ticket history, recent release notes, contract renewal date, any legal/regulatory threads.
4) Initial hypothesis statement (one line): e.g., "Decision delayed due to unmet SLA for ingestion times".
5) Immediate remediation candidates (what we can do in 7 days): call with execs, prioritized bug fix, temporary capacity allocation, draft SOW.

Loss reason taxonomy (use to tag post-mortem):
- Value/ROI: feature gaps, poor business metrics, unmet SLAs
- Adoption friction: integration issues, onboarding failure, onboarding churn after POC
- Relationship & org changes: Procurement delays, executive sponsor left
- Price/Packaging: sticker shock, better competitor pricing
- Security & Compliance: data residency, audit concerns
- Product regressions: performance, quality, hallucinations for NLP use-cases
- Commercial misc: discount expiry, procurement constraints

Timeline template (fill with exact dates/times):
- T minus 90d: Contract/renewal baseline and target metrics
- T minus 60d: Usage trend change begins (metric, delta)
- T minus 30d: First proactive outreach documented (channel, owner)
- T minus 14d: Escalation / exec touchpoint or missing
- T minus 7d: Formal renewal decision communicated
- T plus 0d: Loss accepted or final negotiation
- T plus 7d: Post-departure follow-up and asset retention

Example timeline row (copyable):
"2025-06-01 | baseline tokens/day: 1.2M | CSM check-in - no issues"
"2025-07-05 | tokens/day down 42% vs baseline | AE pinged, no reply"
"2025-08-20 | Procurement requested SOC2 addendum | sent to security team (Escalation ID: SEC-332)"
"2025-09-15 | Renewal declined in writing | Reason: competitive consolidation + pricing"

Hypothesis framing (for QBR):
- Statement: "Why did they leave?" (one sentence)
- Evidence list: prioritized bullets, each with a link or artifact id
- Confidence score: low/medium/high (based on artifacts available)

Counterfactual experiments (design at least 2, choose one short-term and one long-term):
1) Short-term: "Immediate repricing + SOW to keep critical workload"
   - Trigger: renewal decline received
   - Goal metric: conversion of renewal to 60% of ARR within 14 days
   - Owner: AE + CSM
   - Risk: sets price precedent
   - Success criteria: signed amendment

2) Medium-term: "POC extension with focused model/latency improvements"
   - Trigger: performance-based loss reason in timeline
   - Goal metric: measured latency improvement in customer environment + renewed pilot
   - Owner: Solutions Eng + Product
   - Experiment steps: dedicated infra baseline, targeted kernel/quantization change, 2-week pilot, side-by-side perf dashboard

3) Long-term: "Packaging shift for friction-prone integrations"
   - Trigger: repeated onboarding failures across >3 accounts
   - Goal metric: reduce time-to-first-value (TTFV) by 40% for new customers in cohort
   - Owner: Product + Developer Experience

Action backlog (populate during post-mortem):
- Action: "Create single-page onboarding checklist for SAML integrations" | Owner: Diego Alvarez | ETA: 2026-02-14 | Status: draft
- Action: "Module-level perf audit for embeddings pipeline" | Owner: Marcus Reed | ETA: 2026-03-01 | Status: todo
- Action: "Pilot one-time discount + SOW play for at-risk renewals" | Owner: Ava Martinez | ETA: 2026-02-22 | Status: in_review

Metrics to bring to QBR (minimum set):
- ARR at risk (USD)
- Net retention delta (cohort)
- Time between first signal and renewal decision (days)
- Primary loss reason distribution (pie) for quarter
- % of accounts with documented counterfactuals executed

Customer-facing templates (use minimally, customize):
- Short note to sponsor: "We saw the renewal flag and want to understand blockers. Can we schedule 30m to review options?"
- Exec ask template: "We propose a 6-week targeted pilot to address X; if benchmarks met, we will extend terms."

Unresolved questions (for WG):
- Do we have an accepted guardrail for one-off discounts at >$250k ARR? Who signs?
- When is it acceptable to shift product roadmap priority to land a renewal? Define SLA for Product involvement.
- What telemetry is required in dedicated deployments to confidently attribute performance regressions to our stack vs customer infra?

Notes to self / working items (choppy, actionable):
- add link to retention cohort workbook (confluence)
- ask legal about NDA for SOW pilots
- embed small table of support ticket IDs related to latency
- tag postmortem with loss_reason taxonomy for QBR rollup

How to use this doc in a QBR:
- Attach the populated timeline and hypothesis to the QBR slide deck as "Churn case study" (1 slide).
- Present: signal -> timeline -> hypothesis -> counterfactuals -> action backlog -> measurable outcome to track next quarter.
- Ask execs for one decision (yes/no) on proposed counterfactual to unblock runway.

Appendix: quick checklist for data pulls (SRE/observability):
- ingress metrics (per-customer token/sec) last 90d
- p95 end-to-end latency by route last 30d
- error rates and model-quality regressions tied to eval harness
- support ticket summary (titles + severity)

Revision history:
- 2025-09-12 Sofia L: initial draft, coarse checklist
- 2025-11-03 Marcus R: added hypothesis framing + triage steps
- 2026-02-08 Ava M: fleshed out counterfactual experiments, added action backlog template

End of workbook.
